metadata.scenario: A home health aide calls the office in a panic because an elderly patient fell and hit their head. The patient is conscious but confused and has a bump forming. The aide asks what to do. The receptionist instructs her to call 911 immediately and stay with the patient.

transcription.text: Thank you for calling CareFirst Home Health, this is Margaret. How can I assist you today? Hi Margaret, it's Helen Johnson. I need help, I'm really concerned. Oh no, Helen, what’s going on? One of our clients just fell and hit their head! They’re conscious but confused. I understand, that sounds very serious. Is the client responsive? Yes, but there’s a bump forming on their head and I’m worried. You need to call 911 immediately, Helen. This is an emergency. Right, I’ll do that right now! Stay with the patient and keep them calm. Can you do that? Yes, I’m right here with them. What else should I do? Monitor their responsiveness. Ask them questions, see if they can answer. Okay, I’ll ask them their name and where they are. Good. If they become unresponsive, you need to try to rouse them gently. Understood. I'm really worried, they don’t seem like themselves at all. I know this is stressful, but you’re doing the right thing. Just keep talking to them. I can see the bump getting bigger. Should I apply ice? Only if it's safe to do so without moving them too much. Safety first. Alright. I'm calling 911 now. Good. Once they arrive, make sure you inform them about the fall and confusion. Yes, I’ll explain everything. Thank you for your help, Margaret. You’re welcome. After this, I recommend we schedule a follow-up visit for the client. Absolutely, I agree. It might be time for a reassessment. Let’s discuss that once the situation stabilizes. Do you have my direct number? Yes, I have it saved. I’ll reach out for the follow-up. Perfect. I’ll be here for you and ready to assist. Thanks again, Margaret. I feel a little better having you on the line. Anytime, Helen. Please take care, and I’ll be here when you need me. Okay, I’ll keep you updated. Goodbye for now. Goodbye, Helen. Stay safe.
